title: Stabilizers, precision, and noise
subtitle: Muon’s asymptotic geometry · Mixed-precision scaling · Spork · DDPM close reading
intro: Three main readings: a stabilizer changes Muon’s asymptotic geometry, quantization leaves persistent error, and Spork improves post-training through specialization and distillation. Briefs retain the remaining research. The DDPM classic connects noise prediction to training weights.

articles.paper: From Spectral to Frobenius: When Muon Loses Its Spectral Implicit Bias
articles.authors: Yongtao Wu · Mahdi Mansouri · Zhenyu Zhu
articles.title: A stabilizer changes Muon’s asymptotic geometry

blocks.text: For separable matrix-linear classification with logistic loss, fixed finite NS iterations, a positive stabilizer and a sufficiently small step, Theorem 1 gives Frobenius max-margin bias. We use the momentum-free case.[1]

Let \(P_K\) apply the K-fold odd polynomial \(p\) to singular values, with \(a_K=(p^{\circ K})^{\prime}(0)>0\). The assumption \(p^{\circ K}(s)>0\) for \(0<s\le1\) includes the standard cubic and quintic maps. Near zero, the key is local linearization:[1]

blocks.label: Original Lemma 1 · fixed K and stabilizer

blocks.text: Descent makes squared gradients summable, hence the GD perturbation is summable. Bounded trajectory distance transfers the normalized limit. A sufficient step is \(\eta\le4\varepsilon/(R^2u_K)\), where \(R=\max_i\|X_i\|_F\) and \(u_K=\sup_{0<s\le1}p^{\circ K}(s)/s\).[1]

blocks.label: Original proof chain · not finite-time equivalence

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: This asymptotic linear-model result does not equate Muon and SGD performance in nonconvex LLM training.

articles.paper: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
articles.authors: Jinuk Kim · Rajarshi Saha · Muhammed Fatih Balın · Youngsuk Park
articles.title: Low-precision error is not just fewer effective tokens

blocks.text: Write forward/backward quantization schemes as \(\psi_f,\psi_b\), and parameters/tokens as \(N,D\). The empirical law separates effective capacity, effective data and persistent optimization error:[2]

blocks.label: Original Eq. 1 · fitted model, not an LLM convergence theorem

blocks.text: \(N\) excludes embedding parameters; \(\rho_N,\rho_D\) rescale effective size, \(\epsilon_f,\epsilon_b\) are persistent errors, and \(E\) is irreducible loss.[2]

Convex, differentiable-loss analysis with bounded second moments motivates nonvanishing forward-rounding and backward-gradient errors. With schemes fixed, the fitted law approaches \(E+\epsilon_f+\epsilon_b\) as model and data grow.[2]

blocks.caption: Tables 3–4: BF16/quantized grids; fit smaller models/budgets, predict loss on held-out quantized runs.[2]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: The roughly 11-fold improvement concerns loss-prediction MSE, not training speed. Compute-optimal precision depends on the fitted law and hardware cost model.

articles.paper: Enriching Domain-Specific Post-Training with Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
articles.authors: Atharv Naphade · Sam Denton
articles.title: Spork: share capabilities, specialize, then distill
articles.evidence: Method, ablations and compute appendix read

blocks.text: Low-success-rate GRPO has sparse signal. Spork warms up on the full dataset, specializes partition teachers, then consolidates into a base-initialized student on student-generated trajectories.[38]

\(D_i\) denotes a partition, \(w\) its sampling weight, and \(T_\tau\) student tokens only. Implementation uses top-k logits and excludes environment tokens. Warmup uses 40 steps with 8 prompts × 8 rollouts.[38]

blocks.caption: Validation selects checkpoints; gains are relative, not percentage points or equal-total-FLOP comparisons.[38]

blocks.label: Original compute approximation · omits attention FLOPs

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: \(P,L,B\) are active parameters, sequence length and rollout count. The 1.25× ratio is per matched distillation step; teacher training is extra. More teachers did not monotonically improve students; a consolidation bottleneck is the authors’ hypothesis.[38]

articles.paper: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon
articles.authors: Kai Ruan · Jinghao Lin · Tao Chen · Ziqi Zhou · Qianshan Wei · Zihe Huang
articles.title: Long-horizon RL: Muon within an asynchronous recipe

blocks.text: Combines single-rollout asynchronous learning, token-averaged loss, truncated importance sampling and auxiliary penalties for repository repair across two model families. The abstract supports a full-recipe training-success gain, not attribution entirely to Muon.[8]

articles.paper: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon
articles.authors: Sifan Yang · Hongyi Tao · Dingzhi Yu · Haomin Bai · Wei Jiang · Silin Gao · Pi Bu · Lijun Zhang
articles.title: Subspace Muon with orthogonal residual correction

blocks.text: PMRC applies matrix sign to projected momentum and restores the orthogonal gradient residual. The authors analyze fixed and refreshed bases; we omit the abstract’s rate because its assumptions and convergence metric have not been checked.[9]

articles.paper: How Inner Optimizers Shape Replica Scaling
articles.authors: Eugene Belilovsky · Stefan Horoi · Edouard Oyallon · Benjamin Thérien
articles.title: Replica scaling depends on the inner optimizer

blocks.text: Under fixed-budget DiLoco replica scaling, pseudo-gradient covariance and batch-dependent noise distinguish inner optimizers including Muon and AdamW. Whitening-based methods perform strongly over 8–96 replicas; this does not eliminate communication costs.[10]

articles.paper: Which Optimizer Leaks Most? Optimizer Implicit Bias as a Training-Data Privacy Controller
articles.authors: Sagi Habani · Yehonathan Refael · Ofir Lindenbaum
articles.title: Optimizer implicit bias as a privacy variable

blocks.text: Relates KKT conditions to training-data reconstruction for SGD, Muon and Adam on MNIST/CIFAR-10. Muon’s reconstructability depends on architecture and regime; Adam’s resistance to the evaluated attacks is not a general privacy guarantee.[11]

articles.paper: Compound p-values for competition-based testing
articles.authors: Junu Lee · Rina Foygel Barber · Richard J. Samworth · Zhimei Ren
articles.title: Compound p-values: aggregate rather than individual validity

blocks.text: Zhimei Ren and coauthors connect heterogeneous/shared-control competitions to compound p-values. Bonferroni controls FWER; BH may incur FDR inflation, which the paper bounds. These are different guarantees.[12]

articles.paper: Spatial Kernel Restricted Canonical Correlation Analysis: Population Targets, Identifiability, and Stability
articles.authors: Zhen Miao · Yilong Qu · Nancy R. Zhang
articles.title: What do spatial association axes estimate?

blocks.text: Nancy R. Zhang and coauthors study skrCCA targets, identifiability and stability. Conditional on locations under a mean-zero model, targets are kernel-weighted cross-covariances; the fixed-direction null variance assumes independence between blocks.[13]

articles.paper: Narrowing the Collaboration Gap, Probably
articles.authors: Mirah Shi · Marcel Hussing · Ira Globus-Harris · Natalie Collina · Aaron Roth · Surbhi Goel
articles.title: Agent communication: probabilities or actions?

blocks.text: Aaron Roth and coauthors compare action messages with calibrated beliefs in synthetic and maze tasks. Biased probabilities can erase the advantage; post-hoc conversational calibration addresses that mismatch.[14]

articles.paper: L3M: A Verifiable Harness and Runtime for Self-Extending and Self-Improving Agents
articles.authors: Carson Eisenach · Robert Joseph George · Vincent Quenneville-Belair · Kate Gwimm · Dean Foster
articles.title: L3M: a verifiable agent runtime
articles.dateNote: First arXiv v1: 2026-10-14 01:03 America/New_York; manuscript dated 2026-09-30

blocks.text: Dean Foster and coauthors use Lean 4 for a runtime and checked invariants, with recoverable state in Git. The abstract reports Terminal-Bench results with safe tools; formal coverage is unaudited here. The manuscript is dated September 30; this is a first-arXiv listing.[15]

articles.paper: Self-Conditioning Enables Deep Sequential Reasoning in Flow Matching
articles.authors: Zeyang Zhang · Linxiang Gao · Meiqi Gu · Xingyan Chen · Minrui Luo · Kaifeng Lyu · Tianxing He
articles.title: Flow matching: more steps need not mean deeper reasoning

blocks.text: Kaifeng Lyu and coauthors show a constant-round parallel simulation of vanilla flow sampling under output regularity assumptions; self-conditioning changes this limitation. The claim is model-dependent, not a blanket impossibility result for diffusion reasoning.[16]

articles.paper: Tail Competition Explains Scaling in Best-of-N Sampling for Verifiable Problems
articles.authors: Taro Yano · Yoichi Ishibashi · Masafumi Oyamada
articles.title: Best-of-N is a competition between reward tails

blocks.text: Sampling a correct answer is insufficient if incorrect answers dominate the reward tail. Extreme-value analysis separates correct-dominant, incorrect-dominant and critical regimes; the abstract does not provide a universal safe sampling threshold.[17]

articles.paper: Exact Scaling Laws for a Random-Features Bigram Model
articles.authors: Julian Enoch · Elvis Dohmatob
articles.title: Capacity-driven scaling in a bigram model

blocks.text: Fixed random embeddings and Zipf token statistics yield tractable width/vocabulary-dependent regret laws, checked on WikiText2/OpenWebText. This isolates capacity, not full Transformer optimization.[18]

articles.paper: Dimension-Free Scaling Laws for Size Generalization: An Exponential Separation
articles.authors: Behrooz Tahmasebi · Melanie Weber
articles.title: Size generalization can have an exponential sample cost

blocks.text: For sets/graphs, polynomial source decay can yield polynomial in-domain error but only logarithmic size-generalization error. An exponential source condition restores polynomial rates; functional assumptions behind the claimed matching minimax bounds remain unchecked.[19]

articles.paper: Scaling Multilingual Mixture-of-Experts: How Language Coverage Changes Capacity and Compute Allocation
articles.authors: Joel Dag · Nikit Srivastava · Hamada M. Zahera · Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo
articles.title: Multilingual MoE: language coverage is a budget axis

blocks.text: Fits active parameters, tokens per language, expert count and language coverage, accounting for repetition, on 26,300 per-language losses from 64 configurations. Reported mitigation from more experts is conditional on the matched settings.[20]

articles.paper: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
articles.authors: Alan Baade · Kyle Sargent · Vincent Sitzmann · Eric Ryan Chan · Justin Johnson · Li Fei-Fei · Gordon Wetzstein
articles.title: Count tokenizer and generative-model FLOPs together

blocks.text: Generative representation learning uses information differences between conditional predictions to build tokenizers and studies joint compute efficiency. ImageNet/GPIC FLOP extrapolations should not be read as measured end-to-end speedups.[21]

articles.paper: More Than Seeing: Vision as Scalable Anchors in Native Multimodal Pre-Training
articles.authors: Haoyuan Wu · Aoqi Wu · Jiani Hu · Bei Yu
articles.title: Visual gains need not lower text-only loss

blocks.text: Content-free padding replaces image embeddings as a control. Visual content improves image-text prediction with approximately power-law compute gains, without materially changing the text-only loss floor or optimal model/data balance; gains vary by task.[22]

articles.paper: Data Density Scaling Laws for Image Self-Distillation
articles.authors: Alvard Barseghyan · Ani Vanyan · Hakob Tamazyan · Hrant Khachatrian
articles.title: Repeating a smaller dataset can sometimes win

blocks.text: Image self-distillation depends jointly on unique examples and repetition. A modified Chinchilla-style fit helps in some regimes but inconsistently across datasets; deduplication is not uniformly beneficial.[23]

articles.paper: Scaling Cheap Synthetic Pretraining Improves Indoor Radio-Map Prediction
articles.authors: Khoren Petrosyan · Artashes Mkrtchyan · Rafayel Mkrtchyan · Hrant Khachatrian · Theofanis P. Raptis
articles.title: Extrapolating cheap synthetic data for radio-map prediction

blocks.text: Pretrains ResNet-101/Swin-T on up to 128M synthetic examples. Laws fitted at 2M–16M predict downstream normalized RMSE at 32M–128M; simulator mismatch remains a transfer limitation.[24]

articles.paper: Articulation Upper Bounds for Language Models
articles.authors: Alexander Spangher · Daniel E. Ho · Diyi Yang · Noah Goodman · Sanmi Koyejo
articles.title: Scaling curves for concept transmissibility

blocks.text: Optimized messages and prompt recovery probe 1.2k concepts as model capacity grows. Apparent plateaus are observational and sender/receiver-relative, not absolute limits of human language.[25]

articles.paper: Compare to Correct: Pairwise-Guided Logit Adjustment for LLM Test-Time Scaling
articles.authors: Cong Hua · Qianqian Xu · Zitai Wang · Zhiyong Yang · Shilong Bao · Linchao Zhang · Qingming Huang
articles.title: PGLA: correct voting logits with pairwise comparisons

blocks.text: Combines pairwise evidence and vote support in a KL-regularized objective, evaluated on seven models and ten reasoning benchmarks. Full equal-inference-budget comparisons have not been checked.[26]

articles.paper: Input-Conditioned Search for Efficient Test-Time Scaling of Recursive Reasoners
articles.authors: Haochen Shi · Tianwen Fu · Qianggang Ding · Yinhan Lu · Yizhan Li · Huan Zhang · Yajie Zhao · Xingdi Yuan · Hengyang Lu · Bang Liu
articles.title: Recursive reasoning: change the update map

blocks.text: ICS searches input conditions at the same latent state to induce alternative update maps without training. Six-task FLOP comparisons do not imply a universal 100-fold speedup.[27]

articles.paper: SHELDON: Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces
articles.authors: Harshit Joshi · Priyank Shethia · Monica S. Lam
articles.title: SHELDON: search hypotheses and observations jointly

blocks.text: Separates observation discovery from current hypotheses, using unexplained observations to guide search across diagnosis, abstract reasoning and optimization. The abstract does not fully specify comparator inference budgets.[28]

articles.paper: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
articles.authors: Zheye Deng · Sha Li · Changlong Yu · Xin Liu · Qin Lu · Priyanka Nigam · Yangqiu Song
articles.title: ARBITER: counterexamples for code selection and refinement

blocks.text: Trains an agentic verifier to produce checkable counterexamples for code selection and revision. The IOI case uses official submission limits; this is evidence under a specific inference-budget protocol, not a universal scaling exponent.[29]

articles.paper: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation
articles.authors: Ian Magnusson · Noah A. Smith · Pang Wei Koh
articles.title: COUNT: move capacity into host-memory n-gram counts

blocks.text: Uses offline n-gram counts to combine existing unembeddings without added learned parameters. Fixed-compute 1B pretraining and table-swapping adaptation separate host-storage capacity from GPU compute.[30]

articles.paper: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
articles.authors: Zefeng He · Yunkai Chai · Xiaoyang Chen · Tong Zhu · Zongliang Wu · Yun Luo · Yafu Li · Yu Cheng
articles.title: LatentLoop: unequal budgets across shared-block visits

blocks.text: Compresses the first visit’s sequence, retains full resolution on the second and reallocates compute to width. Across fifteen 1.3B–7B configurations, 19.0%/7.9% fixed-NLL savings are fitted predictions against two baselines.[31]

articles.paper: What Do Foundation Models for Market Microstructure Learn? A Controlled Study with Synthetic Limit Order Books
articles.authors: Fernando Acero
articles.title: Negative result: more tokens do not replace regime diversity

blocks.text: In synthetic limit-order books with known latent states and Bayes predictors, capacity/tokens saturate early and regime diversity governs transfer. The conclusion concerns the controlled simulator family.[32]

articles.paper: Counterfactual Gate-Support Decomposition: Separating Selection from Redistribution in Training-Data Filtering
articles.authors: Hyojung Han · Jongmin Kim · Seung-Hun Jeon
articles.title: Data filtering: selection versus redistribution

blocks.text: A four-arm budget-matched design separates within-support selection, redistribution and interaction. Finite pools may make the design unconstructible; unresolved components in retrieval experiments are not evidence of zero effect.[33]

articles.paper: Taming Softmax at the Limits of Muon: A Unified Approach through Hilbert Geometry
articles.authors: Aditya Somasundaram · Charles Guille-Escuret · Alexander Moreno · Zhengzhong Liu · Eric Xing
articles.title: Softmax geometry: Hilbert distance connects RowNorm and Muon

blocks.text: Linear-output RMS movement need not track softmax distribution change. Hilbert-distance constraints connect a RowNorm approximation for LM heads with Compositional Muon for query–key updates; this is a unifying account, not a new large-scale benchmark.[34]

articles.paper: Revisiting the 16x Pretraining Compute Gap between Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
articles.authors: Guanghan Wang · Bing He · Zhan Shi · Benoit Dumoulin · Hanqing Lu · Volodymyr Kuleshov
articles.title: The diffusion-LM “16× gap” depends on the protocol

blocks.text: A roughly 1,700-model study changes likelihood evaluation, block diffusion and encoder–decoder architecture. Reported compute gaps depend on block size; training savings at smaller blocks cannot simply be combined with full-parallel decoding benefits.[35]

articles.paper: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents
articles.authors: Jianghong Zhou · Hao Rong · Chen Lin · Daoan Zhang
articles.title: Memory reuse is constrained by verification budgets

blocks.text: Treats cached reasoning as contraction and studies stale memories after facts change. Under outcome-only verification per memory, certification load and Zipf demand determine safe-reuse scaling; this is not an unconditional bound for arbitrary agent memory.[36]

articles.paper: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training
articles.authors: Paul Setinek · Fabian Paischer · Nils Thuerey · Johannes Brandstetter · Felix Koehler
articles.title: PDE surrogates: budget the compute used to generate data

blocks.text: Jointly chooses sample count and simulation fidelity across six PDE problems, four surrogate architectures and over 7,000 runs. The reported up-to-6.3-fold saving concerns data-generation compute, not the full training pipeline.[37]

articles.paper: Meta’s Generative Ads Model (GEM): Scaling the Central Model and Compute Engine for Frontier Ads AI
articles.authors: Huayu Li · Darren Liu · Xiaoyi (Leo) Liu · Ellie Wen · Jackie (Jiaqi) Xu · Chunzhi Yang · Reva Srinivasan
articles.title: GEM: jointly scaling context, capacity and systems efficiency
articles.dateNote: 2026-10-13 · official technical blog; underlying older papers are not new submissions

blocks.text: Reports longer-history scaling, sparse attention and structured representations transferred downstream. End-to-end MFU is 20–25%; CompSkip’s 43% refers to FLOPs reduction. Architecture, precision, kernels and parallelism change together, preventing single-algorithm attribution.[39]

classic.authors: Jonathan Ho · Ajay Jain · Pieter Abbeel
classic.title: DDPM: one conditional mean, different training weights
classic.dateNote: Historical classic: first posted 2020-06-19; read v2 dated 2020-12-16; NeurIPS 2020 [5]
classic.evidence: Sections 2–4, Table 2 and Appendix B read

recognition.label: Highly cited · 5,441 citations in the checked OpenAlex record (2026-10-15)

classic.question: With network size and training FLOPs fixed, can jointly choosing the time-sampling distribution and MSE weights reduce finite-step sampling error, rather than only training noise MSE?

blocks.title: Background · earlier work
blocks.text: Sohl-Dickstein et al. (2015) learned a reverse process after forward corruption; Song–Ermon (2019) learned scores at multiple noise levels. DDPM (2020) connects Gaussian reversal to noise regression.[6,7,3]
For \(x_0\sim q_0\), fix \(\beta_t\in(0,1)\), \(\alpha_t=1-\beta_t\) and \(\bar\alpha_t=\prod_{s=1}^t\alpha_s\). Gaussian composition gives direct training samples:[3]
Fix reverse variance \(\sigma_t^2I\). Noise prediction parameterizes the reverse mean; sampling starts from a standard Gaussian and follows these reverse transitions.[3]
For \(t\ge2\), the Gaussian posterior KL becomes weighted noise MSE, with parameter-independent \(C_t\). The discrete image decoder at \(t=1\) is handled separately.[3]
The simplified objective drops these time weights, reallocating fitting effort across noise levels rather than preserving the original ELBO.[3]

Our supplementary derivation: squared loss has the conditional mean as its unlimited-capacity optimum. Differentiating the Gaussian-corruption density yields the score identity. This explains the denoising direction, without guaranteeing exact realization by a finite network.

blocks.label: Our derivation · conditional mean and score

blocks.caption: Original Table 2: unconditional CIFAR-10, fixed isotropic reverse variance, T=1000; IS/FID use 50,000 samples. This compares sample quality, not training speed.[3]

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: With unlimited capacity, positive weights can share the same per-time conditional mean; a finite shared network can distribute errors differently. The latter is our interpretation, not a general theorem from the paper.
